full_judgment:
2. The opposite party as plaintiff filed Family Suit No.22 of 1995 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Senbagh, Noakhali, against the petitioner and the proforma opposite parties stating inter alia that on 13.3.90 marriage was solemnized between the petitioner and the opposite party No.1 according to Muslim Shariah Law in consideration of TK.50,000/- as dower money and out of which TK. 20,000/- was fixed as prompt dower and TK.20,000/- was fixed as deferred dower and TK.10,000/- was treated as paid up to the opposite party wife and TK.600/- was fixed as maintenance allowance. Out of the wedlock a daughter was born to them and as there was maladjustment and misunderstandings between the husband and the wife, the husband, the present petitioner, divorced his wife, opposite party No.1, on 12.3.95 and subsequently the wife as plaintiff filed a suit for dower and continuous maintenance. Defendant No.1 filed a written statement denying the material allegations made against him. The suit was decreed exparte. Against the said exparte judgment and decree, the petitioner filed a Miscellaneous Case in the Court of Assistant Judge, Senbagh, Noakhali being Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1997 for setting aside the said exparte decree which was dismissed for default. Thereafter, on 8.3.98 the petitioner preferred Family Appeal No.7 of 1998 in the Court of District Judge, Noakhali with an application for condonation of delay of 80 days. The delay was not condoned and the appeal was dismissed. 

 4. Mr. Md. Nurul Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been serving in Dhaka Electric Supply Department at Tejgaon which is an essential service and so he could not manage to get leave from the authority and go to Noakhali to file the appeal in time. He further submits that on earlier occasions also, the petitioner filed hazira and was present in the Court and when the matter was taken up for hearing he went to call his engaged lawyer who was on his legs in an-other court and could not return to the Court in time as a result of which his Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1997 was dismissed. In support of his contention he referred to Annexure-C. He next draws my attention to the exparte 

 judgment and decree passed in Family Suit No.22 of 1995 and submits that the learned Family Court most illegally passed the order directing the petitioner for payment of maintenance to his divorced wife continuously, and the Family Court thereby knocked down the traditional Muslim Law as to maintenance of a divorced wife prevalent lawfully and legitimately for centuries. This decision of the trial court, according to the learned lawyer appearing on behalf of the petitioner is most ill-considered and ill-conceived as it apparently failed to take into consideration not only the whole conspectus of Muslim law relating to marriage and divorce but even the various verses of the Holy Quran on divorce. In support to his contention the learned lawyer referred to the decision as taken in the case of Hefzur Rahman Versus Shamsun Nahar Begum as reported in 4 B.L.C.(AD) page 14. The learned lawyer submits that the petitioner has complied with the direction of this Court and has paid the entire dower money and the maintenance allowance to opposite party No.1. He next submits that the learned District Judge should have condoned the delay and restored the case, considering the apparent illegality committed by the trial court while passing the exparte judgment and decree which is absolutely against the decision of the Appellate Division. The learned lawyer lastly submits that the petitioner will suffer irreparable loss if the matter is not sent back on remand. 

 5. Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 frankly submits that although there is apparent illegality in the ex-parte judgment and decree of the Family Court so far as it relates to the direction given to the defendant to pay the plaintiff a sum of TK. 600/- per month continuously in future, but many opportunities were given to the defendant petitioner for the redress of the same and on every occasion he failed to appear before the court in time as a result of which his Miscellaneous case filed for setting aside the exparte decree and to restore the suit for re-hearing was dismissed. He next submits that the lower appellate court has rightly rejected the prayer of the petitioner for condonation of delay as there was an admitted delay of 80 days. He further submits that the petitioner has intentionally refrained from appearing before the Court when the matter was taken up and subsequently filed the appeal before the District Judge with an application for condonation of delay only to harass the petitioner unnecessarily. The petitioner miserably failed to show any cogent ground for the delay in preferring Family Appeal case and the learned Court rightly rejected the application for condonation of delay and the appeal. 

 6. I have perused the revisional application along with the annexures and heard the learned lawyers appearing on behalf of the petitioner and the opposite party. It appears that the suit was decreed exparte directing the present petitioner to pay TK. 40,000/- as dower money to the plaintiff and TK. 4800/- as maintenance allowance for the Iddat period and other maintenance, total amounting to TK. 46,800/-, and it was further decreed that the petitioner would pay his minor daughter a sum of TK. 600/- per month till she attains the age of puberty and that a sum of TK.600/- is to be paid to the plaintiff by the defendant, present petitioner, as maintenance allowance for the future. The petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1997 for setting aside the exparte decree and for restoration of the suit but it was dismissed for default on two occasions and subsequently appeal was filed with an application for condonation of delay of 80 days. I find from the record that the petitioner has paid the entire dower money along with some maintenance allowance to his divorced wife as per the direction of this Court and it is also evident from Annexure-C that he filed his hazira before the Court when the Miscellaneous case was taken up for hearing on 19.11.97 (Annexure-C). It is believable that there was no negligence on his part as he was present but he could not bring his lawyer to the court on time for which the case was dismissed. The only ground taken, for condonation of delay was that the petitioner being an employee of Electricity Supply Department, the service of which is declared as essential, it was difficult for him to get leave quickly when needed, is quite cogent to me. The last portion of the judgment passed by the Family Court directing the defendant to pay continuous maintenance allowance to the plaintiff in future is apparently illegal which is against the Personal Law set up by the Muslim jurists and the judgment passed by our Appellate Division. Muslim Law does not recognise any obligation on the part of a man to maintain a wife throughout her life time whom he had divorced.
